title: Proper Drain Pitch & Pipe Support
description: A proper drainage system relies on gravity and rigid structural support to move wastewater effectively. When horizontal DWV (Drain-Waste-Vent) pipes lack correct hanger spacing, the weight of standing water causes the pipe to sag over time—creating a pipe belly. Solid waste and sediment collect in these low sections, causing recurring blockages and placing stress on solvent-welded joints. Professional plumbing installation ensures a consistent downward slope—typically 1/4 inch per foot for pipes under 3 inches—and code-compliant hanger support. Check accessible drain lines in crawlspaces or basements to confirm continuous support.

visual_story: The visual highlights the physical relationship between drain pipe support and proper line slope. Viewers observe a realistic horizontal PVC waste line secured to floor joists with metal hangers. The image visually demonstrates correct alignment, showing how proper hanger placement prevents sagging (pipe belly) and ensures waste moves continuously by gravity without pooling.

on_image_text.hook: Sagging Drain Lines Cause Silent Clogs
on_image_text.explanation: Inadequate pipe hanger spacing creates low spots where wastewater settles and solid debris collects.
on_image_text.takeaway: Maintain code-compliant hanger spacing and consistent downward slope on all horizontal drains.
